title: Stochastic launch confidence ledger and KPI runway
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a probabilistic approach to launch readiness: instead of a single pass/fail checklist, we score readiness across scenarios using Monte Carlo sampling of traffic, error-rate, and capacity noise. The intent is to provide a confidence distribution for go/no-go decisions, staffing, and capacity commits.

High-level idea:
- Convert deterministic signals (SLO pass, test coverage, infra capacity, customer escalations) into stochastic inputs with observed variances.
- Run N simulations (default 2,000) to produce percentile outcomes for latency, cost burn, SLO breach probability, and error-incident counts.
- Surface the P(>=SLO breach) for the next 24/72/168 hours under expected traffic ramps.
- Map percentiles to discrete operational actions (green/yellow/red lanes) and staff/equipment commitments.

Definitions (signals -> distributions):
- Traffic ramp: baseline lambda (requests/min) with daily CV (coefficient of variation) = 0.18 by default; scenario modifiers for marketing spikes (+30% CV) or partner promos (+80% CV).
- Token cost per request: mean from billing forecast, stdev 6% to capture variability in prompt lengths.
- Per-request p95 latency: modeled as lognormal with mu from last 7-day p95, sigma derived from hourly variation.
- Infra failure events: Poisson process with lambda estimated from last 90 days.

Core outputs we track (KPI runway):
- P(SLO breach in next 72h) -> target < 2% for green, 2–12% yellow, >12% red.
- Median and 95th percentile latency under simulated load.
- Estimated token spend vs committed capacity (24h/72h).
- Expected number of incidents (SEVs) per simulation window.
- Probability that queue/backlog > max_allowed for more than 10 minutes.

Sample tracker table (tabular fields represented as plain lines for Drive doc):
- scenario_id | scenario_label | traffic_multiplier | P_breach_72h | median_latency_ms | p95_latency_ms | est_token_spend_72h | est_sevs_72h | action_reco
- S1 | baseline | 1.0 | 0.8% | 280 | 820 | $3.1k | 0 | green: go
- S2 | marketing-nudge | 1.4 | 5.6% | 340 | 1280 | $4.6k | 1 | yellow: partial roll, monitor 6h
- S3 | partner-burst | 2.5 | 28.3% | 620 | 2100 | $9.8k | 3 | red: delay or apply throttles + add capacity

Decision rules (how to interpret percentiles):
- If P_breach_24h > 10% OR median token spend > 110% of committed capacity -> postpone full public ramp; allow closed beta with throttles.
- If P_breach_72h in [3%, 10%] -> open in phased cohorts with live traffic canary and 2x on-call coverage for first 48h.
- If P_breach_72h < 3% AND p95_latency_simulated < target_p95 -> proceed to broad rollout with standard oncall.

Operational playbook snippets (short actionable items):
- Pre-roll (T-48h): snapshot model pins, lock rollout policy, ensure canary route configured (5% traffic), queue up autoscale thresholds + pre-warm GPUs if S2+ scenarios probable.
- During roll (T+0 to T+24h): run simulations every 3 hours with live telemetry; update P_breach metrics and notify traffic-ops channel if percentile crosses yellow.
- Escalation (if red): trigger capacity-reserve order, enact immediate partial-throttle policy, enable degraded-model variant and route 50% to fallback.

Checklist (compact, meant for quick scan):
- [ ] Canary configured and smoke tests passing
- [ ] Simulation inputs refreshed with last-24h telemetry
- [ ] Capacity commit preapproved for top-2 scenarios
- [ ] Oncall rota double-covered for first 48h
- [ ] Customer comms draft ready for outage/latency notices
- [ ] Rollback playbook validated and practiced in staging

Integration notes (where to plug this in):
- A lightweight runner script (prodops/sim-runner) will pull last-90-day metrics from Observability and billing forecast from Finance. Outputs are CSVs that feed a simple dashboard in Console -> "Launch Confidence".
- Alerting: create a metric alert for P_breach_24h > 5% to notify product-ops and s-reliability.

Open questions & next steps (work-in-progress):
- Need to calibrate sigma for latency distributions per model family (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder). Who on Applied ML can own profiling? (cc: Marco)
- Decide default simulation N (2k vs 5k) — performance vs stability of percentiles.
- Add user-impact weighting to incidents (not all SEVs equal). Propose simple weight mapping (SEV1=1.0, SEV2=0.4, SEV3=0.1).

Notes on interpretation / cautionary items:
- This is not a guarantee; probabilistic outputs are conditioned on the fidelity of inputs. Garbage-in -> garbage-out. Use the tool to compare scenarios and make risk-informed tradeoffs rather than absolute thresholds.
- The model assumes independence between some signals (e.g., token length variance vs infra failure). Where correlations are known, we should encode them.

Appendix: quick commands and artifacts
- How to run local (dev) simulation: python prodops/sim_runner.py --window 72 --N 2000 --scenario baseline
- Dashboard proto: /console/launch-confidence (WIP)
- Reference tickets: JIRA-4523 (simulation infra), JIRA-4601 (canary routing), PR#78 (sim runner basic impl)
